newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes firmer, propped by gas oil.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes firmer, propped by gas oil.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures ended Thursday on a firmer note as strength in the gas oil market pulled energy prices higher, traders said.
December Brent stood at $22.25 a barrel by the close, ten cents up after a day of volatile business which saw a peak at $22.48 and a low of $22.12.
November gas oil earlier closed $3.75 a tonne higher at $218.75 after reaching an intraday high of $222.25.
"Brent was been all over the place towards the end and has been trying to find some direction," one broker said.
"It tested $22.12 and then rallied and I think we are looking quite constructive as we move into winter."
Brokers said some of gas oil's strength and volatility was a result of squeeze play on the November contract, which expires on Tuesday.
Signs of good cold weather demand for heating oil in Germany provided a bullish backdrop.

Dealers in London said Asian markets had earlier provided fundamental support for gas oil, as it was thought possible high gas oil prices in Asia may provide an arbitrage outlet for surplus product delivered on expiry.
The December gas oil/Brent crack spread was $5.77 a barrel, almost a dollar higher than on Tuesday.
